newsitem.title: UK: Analyst sees Eurotunnel debt deal soon.
newsitem.headline: Analyst sees Eurotunnel debt deal soon.

text.p: An analyst specialising in high yield securities, Mary-Ellen Collins of BDS Securities, said on Monday she was confident Anglo-French Eurotunnel Plc/SA would settle terms of a debt restructuring deal in a short time.
"I am confident that a deal could be put together, maybe today, maybe by the end of the month," Collins told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.

She said that many securities market players saw the most likely deal as involving an immediate debt-for-equity swap that dilutes existing shares by 50 perecent initially, "with some further dilution possible though convertible bonds".
Collins added she believed that once a deal was agreed Eurotunnel should be able to start repaying interest as soon as the agreement is signed -- possibly around mid-1997.

Provided a sensible form of restructuring was approved, she added, "this will be a very interesting stock". However, from an investment point of view she said the company's financial structure would have to be fixed first.

A spokesman for the company's small shareholders in France, Didier Renaudin, told the same programme that he felt the key factor from the current equity holders' point of view would be the point at which the swap from equity to debt took place.
Eurotunnel's shares were suspended on Monday morning, at the company's request, pending a further announcement and in order to prevent speculation.
Its two court-appointed mediators, who have been helping negotiate with its bankers, are due to hand in their report this evening before their mandate expires at midnight.

On the whole, Renaudin added, he felt the banks would keep working towards a deal. "I don't see any interest for the banks not to do a deal," he said, adding that if the company went into French receivership, banks would face a long wait for any money.
